title: Benchmark Smokewave Iteration - run notes & action items
content:
Meeting: Benchmark Smokewave iteration run notes
Date: 2025-09-02 (run window 09:00-12:30 PT)
Facilitator / scribe: Priya Nandakumar
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marta, Liu, Diego (+ short presence from ops on hand)
Objective:
- Run a short, high-variance smokewave across representative request shapes to catch any recent regressions introduced in last two weeks. Focus on latency regressions (p95/p99) and throughput cliffs during KV-cache churn and model switching.
Context / why this run now:
- A handful of customer reports of intermittent p99 spikes for medium-length requests surfaced last week (see JIRA-IR-1287).
- Recent kernel-selector bump (v1.9.1) and regen-suite changes in PR #482 landed on canaries; we need targeted quick verification across A100 and T4 pools before wider rollout.
Environment & harness:
- Harness: regen-suite v2.3 smokewave mode (mixed chat + embed + rerank).
- Backends: dedicated-hosted canaries (a100-80gb-pool-3) and spot-T4s (t4-16gb-pool-7) to compare.
- Model set: redwood/3b-open (fp16), redwood/7b-q8 (int8 emulation), and fallback-gpt-compat v0.9.
- Request shapes: short (16 tokens), medium (128 tokens), long (1024 tokens), mixed QPS bursts.
- Config knobs: continuous batching on/off, kv-cache warm/cold scenarios, kernel-selector: v1.8.6 (baseline) vs v1.9.1 (canary).
Run plan summary:
1) Baseline sweep on a100 with kernel-selector v1.8.6 to capture steady-state metrics.
2) Canary sweep on same nodes with v1.9.1.
3) KV-cache cold-start test (invalidate prefix cache, then 5k requests at 200 qps).
4) Mixed-burst test: alternating 1m high-burst (2k qps) with 2m low (200 qps) for 3 cycles.
5) Repeat 1–4 on T4 pool (to catch memory/quantization differences).
Key findings / metrics (high-level):
- Baseline (a100, v1.8.6): p50=18ms (short), p95=64ms (short), p50=120ms (medium), p95=420ms (medium), p95 long steady ~1.2s. Throughput steady at ~3.2k tokens/sec for 7b-q8 across pool.
- Canary (a100, v1.9.1): small median improvements on short tails (p50 down ~6%), BUT observed p99 regressions for medium requests: p99 increased from 760ms -> 1.45s in two of three runs.
- KV-cache cold-start: observed a sustained p99 tail lasting ~90s after invalidation on canary; baseline showed shorter tail (~35s).
- Mixed-burst: throughput dropped ~18% during bursts on canary compared to baseline; queueing time grows non-linearly once batcher qdepth > 8.
- T4 pool: no significant difference in medians, but canary exhibited higher variance under memory pressure (OOM retries surfaced twice for long sequences with 7b-q8).
Anomalies & evidence captured:
- Trace snapshot: two p99 spike traces attached (trace ids in Confluence note). Both show long stall in matmul CUDA kernel selection step before token generation.
- Allocator logs: increased temporary allocations around batcher flush boundary on canary.
- Kernel selector logs: a subset of requests selected a new matmul kernel (matmul-xopt-3) that wasn't used in baseline for medium sequences.
Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel-selector v1.9.1 heuristic picks matmul-xopt-3 for some medium-length shapes; that kernel has a regression causing stalls on certain CUDA driver versions. (high confidence)
2) Batcher flush boundary change combined with new kernel increases temporary working memory, causing GC/eviction and triggering KV-cache churn that amplifies p99. (medium confidence)
3) A scheduling change in regen-suite PR #482 interacts poorly with continuous batching under bursty QPS. (low-medium confidence)
Quick repro notes / how to reproduce locally:
- Use regen-suite smokewave with --force-kernel=matmul-xopt-3 on a100 canary nodes for medium requests at 200 qps; observe p99.
- Replay recorded trace (trace ids in linked confluence doc) with profiler enabled.
Action items (owners & due dates):
- Priya: create a minimal reproducer and run isolated matmul-xopt-3 benchmark across driver versions 525/535 (due 2025-09-04).
- Ethan: bisect kernel-selector commits between v1.8.6 and v1.9.1 to find the heuristic delta; open a detailed issue (GH issue) if repro found (due 2025-09-05).
- Marta: schedule a short infra window to run isolated T4 long-seq stress test with canary image and collect allocator/heapprof logs (due 2025-09-05).
- Liu: add temporary metric (batcher.qdepth, kernel.selected) to observability dashboard and add alert if qdepth>10 for >30s during rollout (due 2025-09-03) — to help detect in-prod occurrences.
- Diego: roll back kernel-selector in canary to v1.8.6 for a small set of customers if p99 persists; coordinate with support (standby) (decision due 2025-09-06).
Open questions / unresolved:
- Which driver versions on customer infra correlate with the reported spikes? Need to cross-check JIRA reports for driver info.
- Is matmul-xopt-3 used only for specific model shapes or also for fallback-compat models?
Notes-to-self / quick todos (choppy):
- reproduce w/ --force-kernel fast (Priya): check perf counters
- add more trace sampling during bursts (Liu)
- ping kernel-selector authors in GH thread about matmul-xopt-3 opt flags
- record exact commit hashes for regen-suite + kernel-selector used in runs (done, put into confluence page)
Attached artifacts / links:
- regen-suite PR #482 (smokewave mode changes)
- Trace snapshots & flamegraphs: confluence.redwood/serving/runtime-benchnotes-2025-08 (attached)
- JIRA-IR-1287 (customer reports)
Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Short async update on progress by 2025-09-04 in the Slack thread; follow-up huddle Friday 09/05 10:00 PT if root cause not identified.
- If root cause confirmed to be kernel-selector heuristic, coordinate rollback + patch release and run a remediation smokewave post-patch.
Summary (1-line):
- Canary kernel-selector v1.9.1 shows p99 regressions for medium requests likely due to a new matmul kernel selection; bisect + repro + telemetry expansion are the immediate follow-ups.
